title: The 6 Best Affirmation Apps for iPhone in 2026
description: The best affirmation apps for iPhone in 2026, compared on what each lets you do with the words, where it reaches you during a real day, and what it costs after the trial: I am, Believe, Innertune, ThinkUp, Gratitude and Anicca, verified against US App Store listings read in November 2026.
markdown:
By Anicca · November 2026

All six of these affirmation apps can sit on the same iPhone at the same time. What you remember afterwards is not what made them different. It is how fast they blur together: the wallpapers change, the fonts change, and underneath sits the same set of sentences about worthiness and abundance, poured into a new gradient every year, wrapped in a subscription, and shipped.

The differences that matter are not in the words. They are in what the app lets you do with them, where it puts them during your day, and what it charges once the trial ends. That is what this comparison measures. If you only want the short answer for iPhone: I am is the biggest library, Believe is the most complete practice, Innertune is the one you listen to, ThinkUp is the one you record, Gratitude is the journal, and Anicca (our app) is the one that puts a new affirmation on your Lock Screen every day.

*Disclosure: Anicca, one of the six apps below, is made by the team behind this site, and it is scored with the same rubric as every other app here. Prices, ratings and platforms come from each app's US App Store listing, read on 11 November 2026 (Anicca re-checked on 10 November 2026).*

## How we judged these

Four questions decided the order:

1. **Can you make it yours?** An affirmation you scroll past is a quote. One you wrote, or recorded in your own voice, or said to your own reflection, is a different object entirely.

2. **Does it reach you during a real day?** Not a spa morning. A Tuesday. Widgets, lock screens, a watch face, notifications that arrive while you are stuck somewhere.

3. **What does it cost after the trial?** All six are free to download. None of them stay free.

4. **Is it still open in month two?** This is the only question that really matters, and it is the one most roundups skip.

Ranked against those four, the order below does not match the download charts. For the longer comparison of eleven apps, with the same rubric, see our [full guide to the best affirmation apps](https://aniccaai.com/blog/best-affirmation-apps-2026-11-05).

## The six at a glance

| App | Best for | Standout | Price/yr |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I am | Sheer scale | Biggest library, 738K US ratings | $60 |
| Believe | The most complete practice | Soul Mirror, voice recording, timed sessions | See listing |
| Innertune | Passive listening | Playlists that run while you sleep | $29.99 |
| ThinkUp | Voice recording, if that is all you want | Record and replay over music | $39.99 |
| Gratitude | Journaling and vision boards | Journal first, affirmations alongside | $30 |
| Anicca | A new affirmation on your Lock Screen daily | Daily Lock Screen cards, no streaks (our app) | $59.99 |

## 1. I am: Best for sheer scale

I am is the category. On the App Store since 2014, 4.8 stars from 738K US ratings (1,243,596 across all storefronts, counted by The Vision Board App in October 2026), and the app most people mean when they say "affirmation app." You pick intentions and categories, and the app sends matching affirmations as reminders through the day; widgets, an Apple Watch app and many themes keep them in view. It is also available on Android.

### Where it wins

Nothing else here has that much social proof, and social proof is a real reason to trust an app with a daily habit. If you want zero decisions and a beautiful sentence appearing on your lock screen with no input from you, I am does that at the largest scale. Premium is $60 per year, $15 per month or $150 lifetime, with a 3-day free trial stated on the listing.

### Where it falls short

The free version shows a lot of ads, and the relationship stays one-directional: you receive affirmations, you rarely make them. There is no journal in the listing, and $60 a year is the highest yearly price in this group.

[View I am on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/i-am-daily-affirmations/id874656917)

## 2. Believe: Best for the most complete practice

Believe organises affirmations by the moment you are in — confidence before a hard day, self-love, calm before sleep, gratitude, mornings, relationships, work and more. It is 4.9 stars from 378 US ratings, read on 11 November 2026.

### What sets it apart

The **Soul Mirror** shows your own face while you say the words aloud, and no other app in this list states anything like it in its listing. You can **record affirmations in your own voice** and replay them, write your own, and save the ones that stay with you. **Timed sessions** with themes, music and calming sounds give the practice a set length, and practice medals mark consistency. Scheduled reminders and home-screen widgets keep a line in view, and the listing states iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch support.

### Where it gives ground

The crowd is smaller: 378 US ratings against I am's 738K, and for some people the crowd is the point. Its in-app purchases are listed under the name Believe Premium+, from $0.99 to $19.99, with monthly plans at $2.49 and $3.99 and a lifetime option at $99.99; the store page does not label which price is an annual plan, so no single yearly price is claimed here. No vision board is stated in the listing we read.

[View Believe on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/believe-daily-affirmations/id1565696391)

## 3. Innertune: Best for passive listening

Innertune is built around listening. You pick a situation — the listing names anxiety and racing thoughts, sleep, self-doubt and negative thought patterns — and it builds a personalised playlist of spoken affirmations over beats for focus, relaxation or sleep, then loops it. It is 4.8 stars from 12,047 US ratings.

### Where it wins

Passive playback genuinely suits anyone already listening to podcasts or ambient audio for hours a day, and meeting an existing habit beats fighting one. The free side states unlimited listening time, a night mode for sleep and daily reminders. Premium, listed at $29.99 a year and $9.99 a month, unlocks AI-personalised playlists, 19 voices, recording in your own voice, offline downloads, and a library the listing puts at 77,000 affirmations in 550+ playlists.

### Where it falls short

Passive is the design and passive is the failure mode: audio playing near you is not the same as deciding to mean something. The listing we read is iPhone only and English only, and the features that set it apart are Premium features.

[View Innertune on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/innertune-daily-affirmations/id6443625379)

## 4. ThinkUp: The original voice-recording app

ThinkUp arrived in 2014 and built its reputation on one idea: record affirmations yourself, in your own voice, and play them back over music. Hearing your own voice tell you something is a materially different experience from reading it in someone else's font, and ThinkUp got there first. It is 4.7 stars from 7,519 US ratings, at $7.99 a month, $39.99 a year or $99.99 for life, with a 1-week free trial stated on the listing.

### Where it wins

Own-voice recording is the core of the app, not an add-on. The free version lets you record up to three affirmations with one default background music track, the listing offers 300+ affirmations for 10+ life goals as a starting list, and practice time can be tracked in the Health app as Mindful Minutes.

### Where it falls short

That idea is not its own anymore: voice recording now appears in Believe, Gratitude and Innertune as well. The curated library is much smaller than I am's or Innertune's, and most recording freedom needs Premium.

[View ThinkUp on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/thinkup-daily-affirmations-app/id906660772)

## 5. Gratitude: Best for journaling and vision boards

If affirmations on their own have never done much for you, the format may be the problem rather than the practice, and Gratitude is the strongest alternative here. It is a journal app at heart — daily prompts, photos and voice notes in your entries, journaling streaks and guided challenges — with an affirmation section of hundreds of affirmations, a vision board section that turns goals into a video with music, and Android as well as iPhone. It is 4.9 stars, with 45K US ratings (91,810 across all storefronts), at $30 a year or $5 a month, with a 7-day free trial.

### Where it wins

The vision board is genuine, and journaling depth is real: you can write your own affirmations, add music, record your voice and play or shuffle a collection.

### Where it falls short

Affirmations are one module inside a larger self-care product rather than the point of it, there is no built-in voice to read affirmations aloud, and more sounds and session settings need Pro.

[View Gratitude on the App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/gratitude-journal-prompts/id1372575227)

## 6. Anicca: Best for a new affirmation on your Lock Screen (our app)

Anicca puts a **new affirmation on your Lock Screen every day**. Pick your focus for self-love and confidence, and read the day's affirmations as swipeable cards at your own pace. Save the words you want to revisit in your favourites, copy a quote, or share a card as an image. There are 8 background themes, notification reminders, and home-screen and lock-screen widgets. There are no streaks and nothing to catch up on when you miss a day. The full product page is at [aniccaai.com/affirmation-app](https://aniccaai.com/affirmation-app).

### Where it wins

Delivery with no activation cost: the line is already on the screen you check anyway, written to be believable rather than loud. Anicca is free to download; the subscription is titled **Anicca Premium**, listed at $59.99 per year (Annual Premium), $14.99 per month and $6.99 per week, with a Lifetime option at $59.99.

### Where it gives ground

Anicca runs on iPhone only, with no iPad or Android version, no journal, no vision board and no own-voice recording in the listing. Its ratings base is very small so far: 5.0 stars from 1 US rating, and 4.5 stars from 48 ratings in the Japan store, both read in November 2026.

[Get Anicca free](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6755129214)

## Also worth knowing: delivery decides month two

This is where most people underestimate the decision. People are not really shopping for sentences. They are shopping for delivery.

The research backs the instinct. A University College London study on habit formation (Lally et al., 2010) found that automaticity builds through repeating a behaviour in a consistent context, and took a median of 66 days to plateau. Two things follow. The cue matters as much as the action, and month two is precisely when the habit is still being built rather than finished.

The affirmations that stick are never the ones you sit down to read. They are the ones that show up at a stop light, in an elevator, while a build is running. An affirmation you have to remember to open is one you will stop opening around week three. One already sitting on your lock screen when you check the time has no activation cost at all.

Before you commit to any affirmation app, check the widget and lock screen support specifically, because that is the feature that decides whether you are still using it in month two. In this group, I am and Believe cover widgets, lock screen and a watch app; Anicca covers Lock Screen cards and widgets on iPhone; Innertune's listing states no watch app.

## What's free, and what isn't

All six apps are free to download, and all six put their best features behind a subscription. That is the business and it is fine. What is less fine is how hard several of them make it to see the real number before you commit.

On the free tier you can generally expect a limited daily affirmation or two, a small slice of the categories, and basic reminders — in I am's case, with ads. The things people actually stay for, the full library, the mirror, voice recording, unlimited categories and most widget customisation, sit behind the paywall in every app here.

Listed yearly prices in this group run from $29.99 (Innertune) and $30 (Gratitude) to $59.99 (Anicca Premium) and $60 (I am), with ThinkUp at $39.99 and Believe's annual price not labelled on its store page. Before subscribing to any of them, find the annual price rather than the monthly one, check whether a lifetime option exists, and set a calendar reminder for the day before the trial ends. Doing that once saves more than most of these apps cost.

## How to choose

Pick by the way you want to practice, not by the download count.

- **You want the most capable app and the fewest compromises:** Believe.
- **Social proof and the biggest possible library matter most:** I am.
- **You want it playing in the background while you sleep or work:** Innertune.
- **You only care about recording your own voice:** ThinkUp, though Believe does this too.
- **A vision board and deep journaling are central to how you practice:** Gratitude.
- **You want one kind line on your Lock Screen every day, with no streaks:** Anicca.

Then delete the other five. Six affirmation apps on one phone is a way of practicing none of them.

## The app is not the practice

Most of these apps feel interchangeable because most of them stopped at the same idea: show a nice sentence on a nice background. The ones worth keeping are the ones that give the sentence somewhere to land — through your own voice, your own reflection, your own words, on a screen you were already looking at.

That is a smaller promise than the App Store descriptions make, and it is the one that holds up. So pick one and give it long enough for the cue to start doing the work for you. Sixty-six days, if the research is right, though you will probably notice something shift well before then.

The app is only scaffolding. What you are building is the habit of talking to yourself like someone worth believing.

---

*Method: every app above was verified against its US App Store listing before this article was written; the listing values used here were read on 11 November 2026 (Anicca on 10 November 2026) for our [eleven-app comparison](https://aniccaai.com/blog/best-affirmation-apps-2026-11-05), and no figure is stated here that does not appear in that verified comparison. Where a listing does not state a figure — Believe's annual price is the example — this article says so instead of estimating it.*
